demographics.trauma_type: Accidentally caused serious injury to another

Triggers.value: Weapons or objects used as weapons

Memory.value: When I remember the event I feel overwhelming grief
There are parts of the event that I simply cannot remember no matter how hard I try
Sometimes I feel the full emotional intensity of the event without any clear image or memory

vignette: As she sat in front of her computer, scrolling through lines of code, Sofia couldn't shake off the feeling of unease that had been building up inside her for months. It had been a year since the accident, when her mistake as a cybersecurity analyst had led to a serious injury of a colleague during a training exercise with mock firearms. The memory of that day still lingered in her mind like an open wound. Whenever Sofia saw a gun or any object that resembled a weapon, she felt an instant jolt of anxiety, transporting her back to the fateful day of the accident. She would see her colleague's face, twisted in pain, and hear the sound of sirens blaring in the background. These visual triggers had become a daily reminder of her guilt and grief, making it impossible for her to focus on her work. The more she tried to avoid thinking about it, the more her mind seemed to wander back to that moment. As she delved deeper into her memories of the event, Sofia felt an overwhelming sense of grief wash over her. She would remember the feeling of panic and helplessness as she rushed to her colleague's side, the sound of his labored breathing still echoing in her ears. But there were parts of the event that remained shrouded in a thick fog, refusing to yield to her desperate attempts to recall them. This inability to piece together the events of that day only added to her frustration and sense of guilt. Sometimes, without warning, Sofia would be hit with an intense wave of emotions, as if she had been transported back to the moment of the accident. She wouldn't see any images or memories, just feel the crushing weight of grief and regret. These episodes left her shaken and disoriented, wondering what had triggered them in the first place. As the months went by, Sofia found herself withdrawing from social interactions and avoiding situations that might lead to confrontations. She was convinced that if she could only avoid these triggers, she would be able to keep the memories at bay. But it seemed like the more she tried to escape, the more her mind became trapped in a cycle of recollection and avoidance. Sofia's relationships with her family and friends began to suffer as a result. They couldn't understand why she had become so distant and isolated, unable to talk about what was eating away at her. Her work also started to decline, as she struggled to focus on anything other than the memories that haunted her. It was only when she realized that she was losing herself in this cycle of grief and avoidance that Sofia knew she needed help. With a mix of fear and hope, Sofia finally decided to seek professional help, unsure of what lay ahead but knowing that she couldn't continue living like this. As she sat in the therapist's office, waiting for their first session to begin, she felt a glimmer of determination ignite within her – a resolve to confront the memories that had held her hostage for so long and find a way to heal.
